description: Stream timeouts, provider abort wiring, new setting, and bounded condense stream (design A3 + round-3 MEDIUM; plan.md items 7-12). The bundled OpenAI SDK clears its timeout at response headers, so a stalled body can await forever. Nothing bounds the wait between chunks, and the first-chunk wait is a bare Promise.race with the abort signal that leaks a listener per chunk. OpenAiHandler (used by OmniRoute profiles) never forwards metadata.abortSignal to the SDK. The auto-condense summarizer stream (summarizeConversation, reached from attemptApiRequest's manageContext before any request timer) has no timer and no signal of its own. This feature adds src/core/task/streamIdleTimeout.ts, the first-chunk timeout (apiRequestTimeout), the between-chunk timeout (new zoo-code.apiStreamIdleTimeout VS Code contributed configuration, default 300s; NOT a ContextProxy setting, so the Persisted Setting Checklist does not apply and there is no webview change), signal pass-through in openai.ts and base-openai-compatible-provider.ts, and the condense stream bound. Depends on FEAT-001 only through Task.ts already being edited (no API dependency). FEAT-003's interleaved-failure test relies on the idle timeout added here.
steps: plan.md item 7: create src/core/task/streamIdleTimeout.ts with StreamWaitPhase, StreamIdleTimeoutError (readonly phase, timeoutMs; name 'StreamIdleTimeoutError'; message `No data received from the provider for ${s}s (${phase}); the request was aborted and will be retried.`) and awaitWithStreamTimeout(next, { signal?, timeoutMs, phase }). Contract: next.then(onValue, onError) is attached unconditionally and the first settle wins; an already-aborted signal rejects immediately with Error('Request cancelled by user') and no timer or listener; abort rejects with the same message; timeoutMs <= 0 means no timer; the timer is cleared and removeEventListener called on every settle; it never calls iterator.return(). Write src/core/task/__tests__/streamIdleTimeout.spec.ts (fake timers) with the 7 cases in plan.md item 7.

plan.md item 8: in src/api/providers/utils/timeout-config.ts add getApiStreamIdleTimeout() (key 'apiStreamIdleTimeout', default 300, valid 0..3600 finite number, else 300, returns ms). Add the 'zoo-code.apiStreamIdleTimeout' block right after 'zoo-code.apiRequestTimeout' in /Users/celes/sources/celesrenata/menagerie/src/package.json (integer, default 300, minimum 0, maximum 3600, description '%settings.apiStreamIdleTimeout.description%'). Add the English description from plan.md item 8 to src/package.nls.json after line 42, and translations to all 17 src/package.nls.<locale>.json files. Add the getApiStreamIdleTimeout describe to api/providers/utils/__tests__/timeout-config.spec.ts (unset->300000, 0->0, 3600->3600000, -1/NaN/'x'/4000->300000), reusing mockGetConfig and adding no new `any`.

plan.md item 9: in src/api/providers/openai.ts add `private requestOptions(isAzureAiInference: boolean, signal?: AbortSignal): OpenAI.RequestOptions` and use it as the second create() argument at ~190, ~258, ~405, ~440 with metadata?.abortSignal. completePrompt (~342) is unchanged. Add a comment citing design V7 (OmniRoute assumed to cancel upstream on disconnect). In src/api/providers/base-openai-compatible-provider.ts createStream (~107): `const signal = requestOptions?.signal ?? metadata?.abortSignal; return this.client.chat.completions.create(params, signal ? { ...requestOptions, signal } : requestOptions)`. Add spec cases to api/providers/__tests__/openai.spec.ts (streaming, non-streaming, Azure AI Inference, O3 family: second arg carries signal; unchanged without it) and base-openai-compatible-provider.spec.ts (second arg is { signal } with abortSignal; the existing undefined assertion still passes).

plan.md item 10: in src/core/task/Task.ts import awaitWithStreamTimeout/StreamIdleTimeoutError and getApiRequestTimeout/getApiStreamIdleTimeout. In recursivelyMakeClineRequests: `const streamIdleTimeoutMs = getApiStreamIdleTimeout()` after cachedModelId (~3399); replace nextChunkWithAbort (~3417-3440) with `nextChunk(timeoutMs)` = awaitWithStreamTimeout(iterator.next(), { signal: this.currentRequestAbortController?.signal, timeoutMs, phase: 'between_chunks' }); first call nextChunk(0), loop calls nextChunk(streamIdleTimeoutMs). The first statement of the mid-stream catch (~3853) is `if (error instanceof StreamIdleTimeoutError) { this.currentRequestAbortController?.abort(error); void stream.return(undefined).catch(() => {}) }`, plus a NIT-4 comment that tools already run this turn may repeat on retry (accepted). In attemptApiRequest (~5070) use a local requestAbortController assigned to this.currentRequestAbortController, replace the abortPromise/Promise.race (~5120-5134) with awaitWithStreamTimeout(firstChunkPromise, { signal: abortSignal, timeoutMs: getApiRequestTimeout(), phase: 'first_chunk' }), and make the catch's first statement (~5138) `if (error instanceof StreamIdleTimeoutError) { requestAbortController.abort(error); void iterator.return?.(undefined)?.catch(() => {}) }`, then fall through.

plan.md item 10 test: create src/core/task/__tests__/Task.stream-idle-timeout.spec.ts. Copy Task.spec.ts's preamble (typed TaskTestAccess/getTaskTestAccess, vi.mock block, real ClineProvider setup, stubModelInfo), add vi.mock('../../../api/providers/utils/timeout-config', () => ({ getApiRequestTimeout: vi.fn(() => 80), getApiStreamIdleTimeout: vi.fn(() => 30) })) with real timers, stub getSystemPrompt, backoffAndAnnounce and presentAssistantMessageSafe, and spy task.api.createMessage. Write the 4 cases in plan.md item 10 (mid-stream stall -> signal aborted with StreamIdleTimeoutError reason, cancelReason streaming_failed, second createMessage; first-chunk stall -> first-chunk retry; long backoff inside the first next() does not trip the idle timeout; first-chunk timeout aborts the request signal before the controller is cleared). End each loop by aborting the task on the next createMessage call.

plan.md item 11: in src/core/condense/index.ts summarizeConversation (~371-392) add condenseController; link metadata?.abortSignal to it (immediate abort if already aborted, else a once listener, removed in finally); put abortSignal: condenseController.signal in summaryMetadata (still undefined when metadata is undefined); iterate manually with awaitWithStreamTimeout(it.next(), { signal: condenseController.signal, timeoutMs: phase === 'first_chunk' ? getApiRequestTimeout() : getApiStreamIdleTimeout(), phase }). On StreamIdleTimeoutError call condenseController.abort(e) and void it.return?.(undefined)?.catch(() => {}) and rethrow, so the existing catch returns result.error and manageContext falls back to truncateConversation.

plan.md item 11 tests: in src/core/condense/__tests__/index.spec.ts (fake timers) add (a) yields one chunk then hangs -> after advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300_000), result.error contains 'Condensing API call failed', messages are unchanged, and the abortSignal captured from createMessage is aborted with a StreamIdleTimeoutError reason; (b) first-chunk stall -> result.error after 600_000; (c) update the existing 'summarizes without executable tools while retaining cancellation…' assertion to abortSignal: expect.any(AbortSignal) and assert that aborting the outer signal aborts the passed signal. The 'metadata undefined' test still expects undefined.

findings:
New module src/core/task/streamIdleTimeout.ts exports `type StreamWaitPhase`, `class StreamIdleTimeoutError` (readonly phase, timeoutMs; name 'StreamIdleTimeoutError'; message 'No data received from the provider for Ns (<phase>); the request was aborted and will be retried.') and `awaitWithStreamTimeout(next, { signal?, timeoutMs, phase })`. Abort rejects with Error('Request cancelled by user'); timeoutMs <= 0 means no timer; it never calls iterator.return().
Task.ts names: recursivelyMakeClineRequests has `const streamIdleTimeoutMs = getApiStreamIdleTimeout()` right after `const cachedModelId` (~3457) and `const nextChunk = (timeoutMs: number) => awaitWithStreamTimeout(iterator.next(), { signal: this.currentRequestAbortController?.signal, timeoutMs, phase: 'between_chunks' })` (~3477). The first call is nextChunk(0) and the loop calls nextChunk(streamIdleTimeoutMs). The mid-stream catch (~3892) starts with `if (error instanceof StreamIdleTimeoutError) { this.currentRequestAbortController?.abort(error); void stream.return(undefined).catch(() => {}) }` plus the NIT-4 comment, then falls into the unchanged generic path (cancelReason 'streaming_failed', streamingFailedMessage `${t('common:interruption.streamTerminatedByProvider')}: <message>`, backoff if autoApprovalEnabled, stack.push with retryAttempt + 1). attemptApiRequest has `const requestAbortController = new AbortController()` (~5130), assigned to this.currentRequestAbortController, with abortSignal = requestAbortController.signal. The first chunk is `awaitWithStreamTimeout(firstChunkPromise, { signal: abortSignal, timeoutMs: getApiRequestTimeout(), phase: 'first_chunk' })`, and the catch (~5189) starts with `if (error instanceof StreamIdleTimeoutError) { requestAbortController.abort(error); void iterator.return?.(undefined)?.catch(() => {}) }`, then the existing handling. The abort-reason on the request signal is the StreamIdleTimeoutError, so FEAT-003 can tell a timeout from a user cancel via `signal.reason instanceof StreamIdleTimeoutError`.
Imports added to Task.ts: `import { getApiRequestTimeout, getApiStreamIdleTimeout } from '../../api/providers/utils/timeout-config'` and `import { awaitWithStreamTimeout, StreamIdleTimeoutError } from './streamIdleTimeout'`. Any Task-importing suite that vi.mocks timeout-config must now export BOTH functions; today only Task.stream-idle-timeout.spec.ts does (the provider specs that mock it with only getApiRequestTimeout do not import Task or condense).
Task.stream-idle-timeout.spec.ts preamble FEAT-003 can copy: a trimmed Task.spec.ts preamble (typed TaskTestAccess {getSystemPrompt, presentAssistantMessageSafe, safeEnsureModelFetched, backoffAndAnnounce} + getTaskTestAccess with a commented double cast; vi.mock for delay, uuid, execa, fs/promises (readFile -> '[]'), p-wait-for (resolves at once), code-index registry, vscode (getConfiguration().get returns the default), mentions, extract-text, getEnvironmentDetails, RooIgnoreController, i18n (t = key => key), condense (summarizeConversation mocked), utils/storage, utils/fs (fileExistsAtPath -> false)); real ClineProvider + ContextProxy; getState spied to `{ ...await mockProvider.getState(), mcpEnabled: false, autoApprovalEnabled: true, requestDelaySeconds: 0 }`. The timeout mock is `vi.mock('../../../api/providers/utils/timeout-config', () => ({ getApiRequestTimeout: vi.fn(() => 80), getApiStreamIdleTimeout: vi.fn(() => 30) }))` with real timers. createLoopTask() stubs getSystemPrompt, safeEnsureModelFetched (stubModelInfo), presentAssistantMessageSafe, backoffAndAnnounce (resolved), diffViewProvider.reset, getTokenUsage (contextTokens 0) and abortTask (resolved, so the loop's abort path skips teardown). It spies task.api.createMessage. stopLoop() sets `task.abort = true` and returns a stream that throws on the first next(), which ends task.recursivelyMakeClineRequests([...]) through the abort path (it resolves). Helpers: stallingStream(chunks, onStall?) yields chunks and then awaits a never-settling promise; failingStream(error); apiReqStartedRows(task) parses the api_req_started rows' JSON (real Task.say is used, so rows exist).
DEVIATION (test count): the plan's 4 Task cases became 5. Case 4 (abort before the controller is cleared) is checked with an abort listener registered inside createMessage. It runs before attemptApiRequest's cleanup listener, so it sees the field still set. A 5th case covers D2 directly: the field is cleared during the stall, and the first-chunk timeout still aborts the request's signal through the local requestAbortController. openai.spec.ts got 6 cases (streaming, non-streaming, Azure AI Inference streaming + non-streaming, O3 streaming + non-streaming, no-signal unchanged, completePrompt unchanged).
DEVIATION (condense assertion text): condense/__tests__/index.spec.ts does not initialize i18n, so t() returns the key 'errors.condense_api_failed' rather than 'Condensing API call failed: …'. The new cases match /errors\.condense_api_failed|Condensing API call failed/. Test (c) is split: the existing tools test now expects `abortSignal: expect.any(AbortSignal)`, and a separate 'forwards an abort of the caller's signal' case aborts the outer controller mid-stream and asserts that the signal passed to createMessage is a different, aborted signal. The listener is removed in `finally`, so the outer abort must happen during the stream.
Condense: summarizeConversation creates condenseController before its try. It links metadata?.abortSignal (immediate abort if already aborted, else a { once: true } forwardAbort listener, removed in a new `finally`) and passes `abortSignal: condenseController.signal` only inside summaryMetadata (still undefined without metadata). It iterates manually with awaitWithStreamTimeout. The first chunk uses getApiRequestTimeout() and later chunks use getApiStreamIdleTimeout(). With the vscode mock defaults, those are 600 s and 300 s.
timeout-config.spec.ts: `let mockGetConfig: any` and its beforeEach were hoisted to module scope (same 2 suppressions) so both describes share it.
Setting: zoo-code.apiStreamIdleTimeout (integer, default 300, 0..3600) follows zoo-code.apiRequestTimeout in src/package.json. The description key settings.apiStreamIdleTimeout.description follows apiRequestTimeout in all 18 package.nls*.json files.
